page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It runs on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The hardware allocation is dedicated, featuring 1 physical core and 2 threads per core under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU includes 50 MB of L3 cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache, alongside support for AVX and AVX-512 instruction sets.

This instance includes 33 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the E2s_v3 exhibits lower-tier performance metrics. Its single-core stress-ng performance scored 1237.29, placing it in the bottom 25%, while its multi-core stress-ng score of 1627.47 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests also show limited throughput, with uncached read speeds at 14.08 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.06 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also registered in the bottom 10% of tested systems, reflecting a performance tradeoff where memory capacity is prioritized over raw computational speed.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2s_v3 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio within a lower-cost hardware tier, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high CPU throughput. It is best suited for small database operations, caching layers, lightweight web serving, and basic memory-bound tasks rather than compute-heavy applications or large-scale LLM inference.
